doc.title: Alicia Olatuja interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 9, 2018

title: What 'making it' means
summary: She argues success is personal: debt-free, family and career, travel, or unknown but wealthy jazz stars.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: When I was in college, and all us guys who wanted to “make it” in the music business. And I don’t even think we really knew, well what does that mean? We want to make it. Does that have a —
Oh yeah, that’s like making it. Ooh that’s such a good one. These are really good questions, by the way. I’m enjoying these questions.
Well maybe we should cancel your concert and just keep talking.
Do I still get the check at the end? Just want to know.

I’ll work on that. What is interesting, making it means many different things to many different people. I think you have to figure out what making it means to you and not what making it looks like to somebody else, or what somebody tells you making it means. For some people it’s just being debt free. You’re already, how much percentage of America is in debt first of all. So if you could just be debt free you are up in the higher percentage, upper echelon of like Americans and their finances. So maybe that’s somebody’s idea of making it. Somebody else’s idea of making it, a dear friend of mine was that she said she want to be a professional singer but I also want to be married and have kids. Like I don’t want to have to choose. And so she did that. And there was a season that was really, really tricky for her, but she made it work. And she’s, I don’t know, a superwoman. But that is her idea of success. Other people it’s to travel around the world and have no strings attached anywhere. To be able to pick up and go whenever I want and not have to answer to anybody and not have to worry about where I’m going to live and not have to — not, I know I can go to Spain and find an apartment, and if I get tired — like that’s

their idea. Not everybody wants to be Beyoncé. Not everybody even should be, oh my God. You know? So there’s many different ideas of success and I think the sad part is that a lot of times people feel pressure to become as successful as other people say they should be. And success is so many different things. There are people that I never knew of until I got into the world of jazz. Never heard their name, I didn’t even know they existed. And then, but that doesn’t mean that they weren’t successful until I discovered who they were. It’s ridiculous. They were already Grammy award winners, they had houses in foreign countries and houses in America. They could go anywhere they want. They only do a few performances a year and they’re loaded. And I had no idea who they were. Does that mean they’re not successful, because they’re not worldwide household name like Michael Jackson? No. And look what happened to him.
